name: Rabat Beach
hero_subtitle: Atlantic sand below the walls — local beach life and ocean air next to the capital.

overview.title: Ocean air without leaving the capital
overview.p1: Rabat’s beach stretches along the Atlantic below the historic core. It is more local than resort-polished: families, walkers and the constant ocean wind. Swimming depends on conditions and season; many visitors come simply to walk and breathe after a day in the medina.
overview.p2: Combine with the medina walls or a corniche stroll. For calmer water, locals sometimes prefer spots toward Salé or further along the coast.

food.title: Eating near the beach
food.p1: Simple cafés and seafood places near the ocean front. For a fuller meal, return to the medina or Hassan.
food.p2: Beach snacks are casual — not fine dining.
food.li2: Seafood when the catch looks fresh.
food.li4: Hydrate in the wind and sun.

1.title: Swimming
1.desc: Check flags and local advice — Atlantic currents can be strong.

2.title: Wind
2.desc: It is often breezy; secure hats and light items.

3.title: Valuables
3.desc: Don’t leave bags unattended on the sand.

q1.question: Is the beach clean?
q1.answer: Variable by season and section — walk to find a stretch you like.

q2.question: Facilities?
q2.answer: Basic; don’t expect full resort services.

q3.question: Far from Udayas?
q3.answer: Walkable from the medina/kasbah area depending on your exact point.

q4.question: Good in winter?
q4.answer: For walks yes; water is cold.
